name: NEWS2 auto-score and escalation ladder
trigger: Every observation set is saved (nurse entry or monitor feed).
logic: Score RR, SpO2, supplemental O2, systolic BP, pulse, consciousness and temperature per RCP NEWS2. Band the total; any single parameter scoring 3 escalates on its own.
action: Band 5-6 pages the duty registrar with a 1-hour review clock. Band 7+ pages critical care outreach and starts continuous monitoring. Unacknowledged pages escalate to the consultant at 15 minutes.
today: Sister eyeballs the numbers and decides whether to call. Escalation depends on who is on shift.

name: KDIGO acute kidney injury staging
trigger: Any creatinine result, or urine output falling below threshold for 6h.
logic: Compare creatinine to the rolling 7-day baseline: >=1.5x or a >=0.3 mg/dL rise is stage 1, >=2.0x stage 2, >=3.0x or >=4.0 mg/dL stage 3. Urine output <0.5 mL/kg/h for 6-12h stages in parallel; the higher wins.
action: Raise AKI banner on the chart, prompt nephrology referral at stage 2, auto-flag every nephrotoxic drug on the chart for review.
today: Noticed when someone compares today's creatinine to an older result by eye. Rajesh Kumar's doubling took two days to be actioned.

name: Hypoglycaemia detection and protocol trigger
trigger: Capillary blood glucose below 70 mg/dL, or below 54 mg/dL for the severe path.
logic: Grade the episode, check whether an insulin infusion is running, and look back 4h for a preceding dose change.
action: <70 opens the treat-and-recheck protocol with a 15-minute recheck timer. <54 pages the doctor immediately and suspends the insulin infusion order pending review. Repeat episodes in 24h force an insulin regimen review.
today: Treated correctly at the bedside, but the pattern across the night is invisible unless someone reads back through the notepad.

name: Sepsis screen and Sepsis Six bundle timer
trigger: NEWS2 >=5 with a documented or suspected infection source.
logic: Combine NEWS2, lactate, white cell trend and the wound assessment. Diabetic foot infection is treated as a qualifying source.
action: Start the Sepsis Six clock, pre-populate the order set (cultures, lactate, antibiotics, fluids, oxygen, urine output), and show elapsed time against the 1-hour target on the round list.
today: Recognised by an experienced sister, but the one-hour clock is not measured and door-to-antibiotic time is not auditable.

name: Critical result auto-page
trigger: A result crosses a panic threshold: K+ >6.0, lactate >4.0, Hb <7.0, glucose <54 or >500, troponin positive.
action: Page the named owner directly rather than filing the result in a queue. Record acknowledgement; re-page at 10 minutes.
today: Lab telephones the ward. If the line is busy or the sister is at a bed, the result waits.

name: Missed observation alert
trigger: An observation set is overdue against the frequency the patient's NEWS2 band requires.
action: Amber at 15 minutes overdue on the nurse worklist, red plus charge-nurse notification at 30.
today: Gaps are only visible retrospectively when the chart is reviewed.

name: Deterioration trend model
trigger: Rolling window over all channels, recomputed hourly.
logic: Flags trajectory rather than threshold breach: a patient whose NEWS2 is still low but whose creatinine, urine output and temperature are all moving the wrong way together.
action: Surface a 'trending down' marker on the round list ahead of any threshold being crossed. Advisory only, never auto-escalates.
today: Depends entirely on whether the same doctor saw the patient yesterday.

name: Contrast nephropathy prevention bundle
trigger: A contrast study is ordered for a patient with eGFR <45, diabetes, or a prior contrast reaction.
logic: Score contrast-induced nephropathy risk from eGFR, diabetes, age, heart failure and planned contrast volume.
action: Order pre- and post-hydration, hold metformin from 24h before until 48h after with a scheduled creatinine recheck, hold ACE inhibitors and NSAIDs, and offer a non-contrast alternative where one exists.
today: Depends on the ordering doctor remembering. Suresh Patel is on metformin and ramipril with an eGFR of 54 and a CT angiogram booked for tomorrow.

name: Renal dose adjustment and nephrotoxin review
trigger: eGFR changes band, or a new drug is prescribed.
logic: Check every active drug against its renal dosing rule using the current eGFR.
action: Flag drugs needing dose reduction or withdrawal, propose the adjusted dose, and require an explicit override reason to keep the original.
today: Manual cross-check against the formulary, usually only at the point someone notices the creatinine.

name: Metformin hold enforcement
trigger: eGFR <30, lactate >2.5, sepsis flag, or contrast within 24h.
action: Suspend the metformin order, show the reason on the drug chart, and create a scheduled task to restart it once the condition clears so it is not forgotten at discharge.
today: Held correctly most of the time. Restarting it is the step that gets missed.

name: VTE prophylaxis compliance
trigger: Admission, and every 24h thereafter.
action: Confirm prophylaxis is prescribed or a documented contraindication exists. Immobile post-amputation and post-revascularisation patients are high risk.
today: A checklist item that is signed in bulk.

name: Insulin titration decision support
trigger: Each capillary glucose on a variable-rate insulin infusion.
logic: Apply the unit's VRIII protocol to the current reading, the rate of change and the running rate.
action: Propose the next infusion rate with the protocol row shown. The nurse confirms or overrides; overrides are logged for protocol review.
today: Nurse reads the paper protocol table and calculates at the bedside.

name: Ambient voice capture for the doctor's visit note
trigger: Doctor starts dictation at the bedside or immediately after.
logic: Speech to text, then clinical entity extraction into the structured visit template: pain score, pulses, capillary refill, wound dimensions and appearance, impression, and each plan item as a separate action.
action: Pre-fill the template, highlight every extracted value for confirmation, and leave the raw transcript attached to the note. Nothing is filed until the doctor signs.
today: Typed after the round, often hours later, frequently abbreviated.

name: Notepad photo to structured observations
trigger: A photo of the paper observation sheet is uploaded.
logic: OCR the handwritten grid, map cells to observation channels, and score confidence per field.
action: Present the parsed values next to the photo for one-tap confirmation. Low-confidence fields are highlighted and cannot be accepted silently. This is the bridge that lets the unit move over ward by ward.
today: The photo arrives on the doctor's phone over WhatsApp and is never transcribed into any system at all.

name: Structured nurse observation entry
trigger: Nurse records an observation round.
logic: Numeric entry with range validation, NEWS2 computed live as fields are filled, and the escalation prompt shown before the form is saved.
action: One entry serves the chart, the score, the alert engine and the audit trail. Replaces the notepad and the phone photograph.
today: Written on paper, photographed, sent to the doctor, and re-entered later by someone else if at all.

name: Photography prompt at dressing change
trigger: A dressing change is recorded, or a wound's photograph interval lapses.
logic: Each wound carries a capture interval set by its care plan — every dressing change for an active ulcer, weekly for a stable one, and every fifth session for a wound under an HBOT course.
action: Prompt while the dressing is down and the wound is exposed, which is the only moment the photograph costs nothing. A lapsed interval appears on the nurse worklist.
today: Photographs are taken when someone thinks of it, which is usually when the wound already looks worse.

name: Direct monitor and glucometer integration
trigger: Continuous, from bedside devices.
action: Stream monitor vitals and glucometer readings straight into the chart, leaving the nurse to validate rather than transcribe.
today: Read off the monitor and copied by hand.

name: HBOT candidacy screening
trigger: A wound is graded Wagner >=3, or an ulcer passes 30 days without 50% area reduction on standard care.
logic: Check the four gates together: Wagner grade, duration on standard care, perfusion (ABI or toe pressure, post-revascularisation where applicable), and tissue hypoxia. Periwound TcPO2 below 40 mmHg on air confirms hypoxia; an in-chamber study above 200 mmHg at treatment pressure predicts response. Absolute contraindications (untreated pneumothorax, specific chemotherapy agents) are checked against the problem and drug lists.
action: Raise a referral prompt with the gates it already satisfies and the evidence still missing, so the TcPO2 study is booked rather than the referral bouncing. Where a gate fails, record why — deferred is not the same as declined.
today: Referral depends on the consultant remembering to consider HBOT. Patients who would benefit are found late or not at all.

name: In-chamber glucose safety
trigger: Every HBOT session, before compression and after decompression.
logic: Hyperbaric oxygen lowers capillary glucose, typically by 30-50 mg/dL over a 90-minute session. A diabetic patient compressed at the lower end of range can leave the chamber hypoglycaemic, and the early signs are hard to see through a hood.
action: Block the session if pre-session glucose is below the unit floor until carbohydrate is given and the reading repeated. Record the paired pre and post values against the session, and surface a patient whose average drop is widening so the insulin regimen is reviewed before an episode happens.
today: Checked by the chamber technician and written on a paper session sheet that never reaches the diabetes team.

name: Photograph capture standard and quality gate
trigger: An image is uploaded against a wound.
logic: Validate the capture standard at the point of upload: calibration marker present and detected, focus, exposure, and angle within tolerance. Measurement is computed from the detected marker scale, never from pixel dimensions alone.
action: Accept and measure, or reject with the specific fault and prompt a re-take while the dressing is still down. An uncalibrated image is still stored as a clinical record but carries no measurement, and the chart shows a gap rather than a fabricated number.
today: Photographs are taken on personal phones at varying distance and angle, so week-to-week comparison is impossible and nothing can be measured from them.

name: Healing trajectory and HBOT futility review
trigger: Each new calibrated measurement, and at the session-20 checkpoint.
logic: Track percentage area reduction against the expected curve. Failure to achieve 50% reduction at four weeks predicts non-healing and is the point to reconsider revascularisation. At session 20 of a 30-session course, insufficient progress triggers a formal decision to continue, stop, or change strategy.
action: Plot the trajectory against the expected curve, flag divergence, and force an explicit recorded decision at the checkpoint rather than letting the course run to 30 by default.
today: Courses run to completion because stopping requires someone to actively review. A wound that is not responding consumes 30 chamber slots another patient needed.

name: Image consent, retention and disclosure control
trigger: Upload, access, export, and the nightly lifecycle job.
logic: Every image carries a consent scope recorded at capture: direct care, audit, teaching, publication, research. Scope is enforced at read time, not just at upload, because the lawful basis for teaching use is different from the basis for treating the patient.
action: Deny out-of-scope access and log the attempt. Strip embedded EXIF location and device identifiers on ingest. Apply the retention clock, move objects between storage tiers on age, and require de-identification before any export leaves the clinical boundary.
today: Photographs sit in the camera roll of whoever took them and in a WhatsApp thread. There is no consent record, no retention limit, no access log, and no way to withdraw them.

name: Automated tissue composition from the photograph
trigger: A calibrated image is accepted.
logic: Segment the wound bed into granulation, slough, necrotic and epithelial tissue and report each as a percentage of area.
action: Pre-fill the tissue composition fields for the clinician to confirm, and trend composition alongside area. A wound shrinking but converting to slough is deteriorating, which an area-only chart hides.
today: Estimated by eye and described in words that differ between assessors, so the trend is not comparable.

name: SBAR shift handover auto-draft
trigger: Shift change.
logic: Assemble situation, background, assessment and recommendation from the last 12h of observations, new results, medication changes and outstanding tasks.
action: Produce a draft per patient for the outgoing nurse to amend and sign, rather than compose from memory.
today: Verbal handover from a paper list. Quality varies with who is handing over.

name: Discharge summary auto-draft
trigger: Discharge decision recorded.
action: Draft diagnoses, procedures, complications, medication changes with reasons, follow-up appointments and the diabetic foot care plan from the structured record.
today: Written from scratch, often by the most junior doctor, frequently delayed.

name: Coding and billing capture
action: Suggest ICD-10 and procedure codes from the structured note, with the supporting evidence linked for audit.
today: Retrospective chart review by the coding team.

name: Round list prioritisation
trigger: Continuous.
logic: Order the list by acuity, unacknowledged alerts, unread nursing notes and time since last review, rather than by bed number.
action: The patient who needs the doctor first appears first.
today: Round runs bed by bed. The sick patient in the last bed waits.

name: Task and referral tracking
trigger: A plan item is signed in the visit note.
action: Every plan item becomes a tracked task with an owner and a due time. Overdue referrals surface on the round list.
today: Plan items live in free text. Whether a referral happened is discovered at the next round.

name: Step-down and discharge readiness
trigger: Continuous.
logic: NEWS2 stable for 48h, glucose in range, wound improving, mobility documented, no outstanding referrals.
action: Surface the patient as a step-down candidate with the blocking items listed. Mohammed Iqbal has met the criteria for 36 hours.
today: Depends on the consultant noticing during the round.

name: Diabetic foot risk stratification and recall
trigger: Discharge, and at every outpatient contact.
logic: IWGDF risk category from neuropathy, peripheral arterial disease, deformity, and ulcer or amputation history.
action: Set the surveillance interval automatically and drive the recall list. Recurrence prevention is where the readmissions are.
today: Follow-up interval set ad hoc; recall depends on the patient remembering.
